subject: Unit price gap scouting: $/1M targets and host comps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@brightleaf.ai>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask: unit-price targets and host comparisons

Thanks for the call earlier, Liam — good to meet. Quick written recap so we have the same page and we can move to procurement: 

Key notes from today's discovery:
- Primary use case: contextual summarization + search augmentation for customer support (95% read + generate load; average prompt length 420 tokens; avg response length ~220 tokens).
- Expected steady-state volume: 75M tokens / month (generally steady), with peak bursts to ~140M TPM for quarterly campaigns.
- Security: BrightLeaf needs SOC2-comparable controls and a FedRAMP-ready partner for certain clients; will evaluate Private deployment if required.

Pricing signals you gave on the call:
- Budget range: $90k–$140k / month for inference (inclusive of hosting + API).
- Procurement timeline: vendor short-listing over next 2–3 weeks; PO by end of month if numbers align.

Specific asks from us:
1) Can you confirm the steady-state and peak token numbers above? (especially whether 75M/month is firm)
2) Which pricing comparators matter most — is the decision driven purely by $/1M tokens, or do latency / regional hosting / private deployment pricing also matter?
3) Any procurement constraints (required contract term, firewall/IAM limits) that would materially affect pricing?

What we’ll send next (today):
- A short benchmark summary comparing Redwood's target $/1M vs the common hosts (OpenAI, Anthropic, two open-host providers) at the 75M and 140M TPM bands.
- A draft pricing slate for a 3-month pilot + sample PoC SOW (attachment).

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm volumes, we’ll push a targeted price suggestion and an option for a Dedicated pilot that keeps unit economics stable during bursts.
- Schedule a procurement call with your procurement contact — is Friday 12/11 at 10am PT okay?

Thanks — copied Ben and Karthik for pricing + infra context.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126

Date: 2026-12-07T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: unit-price targets and host comparisons

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the crisp summary. A few confirmations on our side: 
- 75M TPM steady-state is what we expect after launch (Q1). The 140M bursts are likely to happen during quarterly feature drops, so we need pricing that doesn't blow up during those 2–3 week windows.
- Primary decision axis: first is $/1M tokens, second is the ability to run in a VPC/private mode for some regulated accounts, third is latency (we need <250ms 95th for customer-facing flows).
- Procurement notes: standard 12-month term preferred, but open to a 3-month pilot with a subsequent annual commit. We require an initial compliance packet (SOC2 Type II, encryption-at-rest, KMS options) before procurement signs off.

Can you share the benchmark file and a ballpark $/1M for the steady-state and burst tiers? If you can show how Redwood compares to OpenAI and Anthropic at our volumes, that will speed internal shortlisting.

Also looping in procurement — procurement@brightleaf.ai for scheduling.

— Liam
Head of Product | BrightLeaf AI
liam.carter@brightleaf.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@brightleaf.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: unit-price targets and host comparisons

Liam — quick benchmarking snapshot (high level) to frame expectations. Attaching the PDF Marissa referenced; below are the key takeaways we shared internally: 

Benchmark assumptions (apples-to-apples):
- Model class: 22B-ish open models vs Anthropic Claude-instruct and OpenAI gpt-4o-preview for commercial comparison.
- Effective token mix: 65% input / 35% output on average for your workload (we used your avg prompts + responses).
- Delivery: hosted API vs Dedicated pool priced separately (Dedicated reduces unit rates at scale but has commit overhead).

Representative $/1M token numbers (rounded):
- OpenAI (hosted): $22.50 / 1M (at this volume they offer some enterprise discounts, effective $/1M can drop to ~$18–20 depending on contract and multi-month commit).
- Anthropic (hosted): $28–32 / 1M (varies by model variant / throughput SLA).
- Typical open-host providers (cloud-hosted open-weights): $9–14 / 1M (varies by quantization + ops overhead; some aggressive hosts advertise sub-$8 but often exclude egress/replication).
- Redwood target (hosted API): $10–12 / 1M steady-state for 75M TPM band; burst-protected pricing at $12–14 / 1M up to 140M TPM.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool): effective unit of $6–8 / 1M with a 6–12 month commit (with predictable throughput and private control plane).

Notes and tradeoffs:
- The open-host numbers look attractive on unit price but often exclude operational guarantees (latency SLOs, multi-zone redundancy) or have significant hidden costs (KV cache misses, cold-start token spikes).
- OpenAI/Anthropic hosted options are straightforward but are materially higher per-unit. They include higher operational guarantees out-of-the-box.
- If a private deployment is required for certain clients, Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment becomes preferred — that shifts the economics (CAPEX/commit vs variable $/token).

If $/1M is the gating factor, the simple way to get to the low single-digit bands is a Dedicated-like commitment or a multi-month prepay. For a fast pilot we recommend: 3-month pilot at $11 / 1M (hosted) with an option to convert to a Dedicated commit that targets $7 / 1M.

I’ll flag that we’ll include the latency and compliance tradeoffs on the attached benchmark PDF. Happy to run a short modeling spreadsheet for your finance team if procurement asks for a direct per-month cost for 75M vs 140M tokens.

— Ben
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
